Families.Name: Walk with shared width and height
Families.Constraint: W and H are joined by an actual equality obligation.
Families.Release: Removing that obligation admits independent widths and heights.

Families.Name: Four-step independent rectangle walk
Families.Constraint: Opposite reaches share roles; W and H are independent; return is checked.
Families.Release: Already permits rectangular aspect changes. A new corner factorization alone adds no range.

Families.Name: Two-step corner repeated by half-turn
Families.Constraint: One horizontal/vertical corner, one half-turn copy, and two declared endpoint joins.
Families.Release: Same sampled rectangle range as the free four-step walk; different reusable construction.

Families.Name: Two pairs of parallel rails
Families.Constraint: Both horizontal rails point right; both vertical rails point up; intersections are shared sites.
Families.Release: Aspect changes fit. A concave notch requires additional structure.

Families.Name: Two routes sharing their endpoints
Families.Constraint: Upper and lower three-step caps share start and finish, retaining opposed route flows.
Families.Release: Same rectangle ink range, but a different directed boundary range.

Families.Name: Four equal-turn radial markers
Families.Constraint: Common contour, cyclic adjacency and equal radial turns; selected calibration requires W = H.
Families.Release: Releasing equal turns allows the selected rectangular calibration to stretch.

Families.Name: Radial markers with angular spacing open
Families.Constraint: Common contour and cyclic adjacency remain; this probe supplies a centered rectangular realization.
Families.Release: Matches rectangle ranges here; this is not an enumeration of all angular placements.

Families.Name: Six phases with a zero-read notch
Families.Constraint: Six ordered phases remain; the supplied N binding is zero at this resolution.
Families.Release: Two participating zero-length phases can expose a notch when the offered N domain expands.

Families.Name: Six phases with notch optional
Families.Constraint: Same six-phase construction; both N = 0 and one shared-reach N are offered.
Families.Release: Includes the sampled rectangles and additional concave outlines without deleting the latent phases.

Families.Name: Six equal steps around a rectangle
Families.Constraint: Right, right, up, left, left, down all reuse one extent role. Every phase uses W twice; H is offered but unused.
Families.Release: Total width is 4W and height is 2W. Varying the unused H cannot broaden this fixed-aspect family; independent corner extents can.

Ranges.Domain: W and H each use 1 through 4 repeated shared reaches (normally half-extents). Six-equal-steps uses W twice per equal phase, giving total width 4W and height 2W; H is unused there. N is a zero-at-resolution publication, or zero/one in notch-range. One common origin, frame and resolution; no translation or rotation quotient.
Limits: Range inclusion and equality refer only to these explicitly enumerated publications, not all possible machine outputs.
Undirected ink ignores traversal and subdivision; directed ink retains segment direction but still ignores execution order. Both preserve overlapping occurrence multiplicity.
Boundary agreement does not establish identical topology, machine, potential, construction history, area prediction or equal probability of outputs.
The radial-open family samples one supplied rectangular realization. Open angular spacing has many other possible realizations that are not sampled.
Six-equal-steps has only one used extent role. Its unused H publications duplicate outputs; finite range overlap is also limited by the offered scale range.
Zero-at-resolution notch phases remain in structure and evidence. Their lack of visible length is not removal of participation.

Samples.Name: Reuse the original, fixed placement
Samples.Rule: Every request reads the original wing through the same reflection-and-advance action; repeated copies overlap.

Samples.Name: Reuse the preceding result
Samples.Rule: Each output becomes the next action's input. Advance accumulates and vertical orientation alternates.

Samples.Name: Reuse the entire accumulated group
Samples.Rule: Keep the current group and add its transformed copy. Section participation doubles per round; coincident copies are not merged.

Samples.Name: Reuse the original with advancing placement
Samples.Rule: The original is unchanged; supplied placement steps advance each copy. A fixed reflection does not create alternating orientation.

Samples.Name: Reflect vertical, then advance
Samples.Rule: The horizontal displacement is unchanged by this vertical reflection.

Samples.Name: Advance, then reflect vertical
Samples.Rule: The same two native actions in the other order; this selected perpendicular displacement commutes.

Samples.Name: Reflect horizontal, then advance
Samples.Rule: The mirror opposes horizontal coordinates before the positive displacement is added.

Samples.Name: Advance, then reflect horizontal
Samples.Rule: The final mirror also reverses the displacement; these actions do not commute.

Samples.Name: Original / mirror cell
Samples.Rule: Two ordered motif positions form a supplied cell. Two placement steps supply its period; a separate cyclic read permission allows wrapping.

Samples.Name: Mirror / original cell
Samples.Rule: Two ordered motif positions form a supplied cell. Two placement steps supply its period; a separate cyclic read permission allows wrapping.

Samples.Name: Opposite phase with an added mark
Samples.Rule: Two ordered motif positions form a supplied cell. Two placement steps supply its period; a separate cyclic read permission allows wrapping.

Samples.Name: The same feedback action on a zigzag
Samples.Rule: The source shape changes; the connected reflection-and-advance action is reused.

Comparisons.Name: Changing which structure is reused
Comparisons.Note: The action is shared, but source dependencies differ. A fixed original accumulates coincident copies, not an advancing strip.

Comparisons.Name: Grouping changes participation
Comparisons.Note: The occupied locations can resemble one another, but the growing group has overlapping multiplicity. Ink is not silently unioned.

Comparisons.Name: Placement is separate from feedback
Comparisons.Note: Both advance across the page. Only output feedback alternates the previous result's orientation.

Comparisons.Name: These two actions commute in this basis
Comparisons.Note: Vertical reflection and horizontal translation agree in either order for this connected frame.

Comparisons.Name: The displacement is reflected too
Comparisons.Note: Horizontal reflection and horizontal advance disagree. Relaxing phase is not permission to discard this changed displacement.

Comparisons.Name: A finite translated crop still has different ends
Comparisons.Note: A one-slot translation aligns the interior cadence but moves the finite cell's end. No crop is silently discarded.

Comparisons.Name: Relax phase under a supplied periodic continuation
Comparisons.Note: One connected placement action shifts the selected phase; its two-step period supplies the validated inverse wrap. This needs the explicit cyclic-cell quotient permission, not forward continuation alone, and preserves every section occurrence.

Comparisons.Name: A changed motif cannot be explained by phase alone
Comparisons.Note: One connected placement action shifts the selected phase; its two-step period supplies the validated inverse wrap. This needs the explicit cyclic-cell quotient permission, not forward continuation alone, and preserves every section occurrence.

Shapes.Name: Square with a shared extent
Shapes.Change: Both extents are joined by an equality obligation.
Shapes.Retains: Ordered loop, four phases, right corners, equal sides.
Shapes.Limits: A rectangular offer is rejected until the equality obligation is released.

Shapes.Name: Rectangle
Shapes.Change: Release W = H; the two opposing pairs still share their respective reach.
Shapes.Retains: Four phases, closure, right corners, opposing side correspondence.
Shapes.Limits: Releasing equality does not remove the turn or closure obligations.

Shapes.Name: Diagonally transformed square
Shapes.Change: Map each H step to H+V and each V step to -H+V.
Shapes.Retains: Equal sides, right corners, ordered closed loop.
Shapes.Limits: This integer-word map turns 45 degrees AND scales by sqrt(2); it is not a unit-length rotation.

Shapes.Name: Rhombus: turn, then stretch
Shapes.Change: Apply the diagonal map, then double only the horizontal component.
Shapes.Limits: Right corners no longer survive. Equal sides alone do not imply a square.

Shapes.Name: Rectangle: stretch, then turn
Shapes.Change: Double the original horizontal component, then apply the diagonal map.
Shapes.Limits: Equal adjacent sides no longer survive. The same two actions in the other order give a rhombus.

Shapes.Name: Sheared loop
Shapes.Change: Add one horizontal step to every upward step, and its inverse to every downward step.
Shapes.Limits: Neither equal adjacent sides nor right corners is preserved here.

Shapes.Name: Extended supporting lines
Shapes.Change: Select the extended supports instead of the bounded perimeter.
Shapes.Retains: Four support directions and correspondence to the source edges.
Shapes.Limits: The four strokes cross in projection; they are not welded. This is not a closed boundary.

Shapes.Name: Diagonal supporting lines
Shapes.Change: Apply the same diagonal map to the four extended supports.
Shapes.Limits: Joining crossings would be an additional topology change.

Shapes.Name: Notched loop
Shapes.Change: Supply a six-phase candidate with a nonzero detour and a checked return.
Shapes.Retains: Proposed width, height and notch role correspondences link the candidate to the source program.
Shapes.Limits: This is an authored candidate association, not an executed edit or a claim of shared site identity. Adding or removing edges needs a structural edit law.

Shapes.Name: Open three-step path
Shapes.Change: Supply a three-phase candidate with no return edge.
Shapes.Retains: Proposed width, height and notch role correspondences link the candidate to the source program.
Shapes.Limits: This is an authored candidate association, not an executed edit or a claim of shared site identity. Adding or removing edges needs a structural edit law.

Shapes.Name: 4 equal contour partitions, joined
Shapes.Change: Subdivide one native circular whole, locate its marks, and join successive marks; return to the first mark.
Shapes.Retains: Shared contour and radial reach; ordered subdivision; explicit adjacency and closing seam.
Shapes.Limits: The regular picture illustrates the declared contour contract. No screen coordinates prove side lengths; the chord-to-planar metric reader remains open.

Shapes.Name: Whole circular contour
Shapes.Change: Select the circular whole itself rather than a list of chords between selected marks.
Shapes.Retains: Point-derived common offset, radial attachment, whole traversal and closing site.
Shapes.Limits: A native contour is present; this does not claim that dropping a polygon's side count generates a circle.

Findings: A weaker equality obligation broadens a range; a different view need not broaden it.
Stretch and diagonal reorientation preserve different constraints when their order is exchanged.
Four equal contour partitions give the square candidate. A rectangle can use unequal alternating angular gaps on the same circle; an ellipse is not required.
A five-sided boundary requires another marker and edge plus a different turn partition. It is not merely a four-side binding made unknown.
The whole circle is an intrinsic construction, not an increasingly dense polygon.
Coordinates are a selected rendering/read basis. Copying a candidate does not transfer material or alter the source.
